ordinances.title: Collection, storage, sharing, and destruction of captured license plate data for law enforcement purposes; penalty
ordinances.summary: Statewide rule for law-enforcement automated license plate readers. Enacted in 2018 by HB 79 and amended effective July 1, 2025 by SB 153. Access to captured plate data is limited to a law-enforcement purpose, the default destruction period is 30 months, agencies that deploy a system must keep use and training policies, and captured plate data is not an Open Records disclosure.
ordinances.notes: Section text checked against the public 2025 Code of Georgia page. This is a statute, not a city ordinance. Official compilation PDF: https://www.legis.ga.gov/api/document/docs/default-source/joint-features-document-library/t35-t36-ch1-59-(v27)-2025-pdf.pdf

ordinances.title: Surveillance technology oversight and approval
ordinances.summary: Proposed Atlanta ordinance to tier city surveillance tools, including license plate readers, and require impact reports, use policies, and council approval for higher-impact systems. Public reporting describes introduction in 2026 and a hold in committee; adoption was not shown in sources checked on this date.
ordinances.notes: Introduction also reported at https://www.11alive.com/article/news/community/atlanta-mayor-andre-dickens-surveillance-technology-legislation-flock-cameras/85-515486e0-e235-4225-8ac1-236d4f9c6448. Status is procedural, not an enacted code section.

ordinances.title: Revised technical requirements for mandatory video surveillance systems at convenience stores
ordinances.summary: Adopted February 14, 2024. Amends Chapter 15 of the DeKalb County code to revise technical requirements for mandatory video surveillance systems at convenience stores.
ordinances.notes: This ordinance covers cameras at private convenience stores. It does not regulate law-enforcement license plate readers.
